A maintenance run compacts first, then cleans up, in one fixed order. The order is defined in code and no preset can change it.

Seven operations, skipping the ones a table does not need. Expiry comes after compaction so one run reclaims the space its own compaction freed. Apache Iceberg gives you hidden partitioning, snapshot isolation, schema evolution and engine-agnostic metadata. It does not promise that tables stay fast. Left alone, four things pile up, and each one compounds independently, so fixing one does not fix the others. Rewrites data files so delete files are applied and no longer re-merged on every read. On Spark it passes a delete-file threshold. On Trino it runs as an OPTIMIZE .
Consolidates position-delete files without rewriting data. Spark only, because Trino does not support it.
Partition-aware compaction of small files, planned from stored scan data. This is the step the chunking rules below exist to protect.
Refreshes table statistics straight after compaction, while the new layout is fresh.
Consolidates manifests. Trino calls it optimize_manifests and Spark calls it rewrite_manifests .
Drops snapshots the retention policy would not keep, and the files only they referenced. Guarded, and forcing it is audited.
Deletes files in storage that no snapshot references. Guarded, and forcing it is audited.

A large table is never compacted in one statement. The planner ranks partitions by small-file count, highest first, skips those under the min_small_files threshold, and then picks one of three paths. The planner picks one path per run. A worker asks the governor for permission before it runs anything. The governor probes live load, from system.runtime.queries on Trino and from slots on Spark on EMR, and either admits the job or defers it. It also applies per-replica caps and round-robins across replicas. Scaling workers does not raise the number of parallel rewrites. The governor does. The scanner grades a table from stored metadata. It does not scan data files on the request path, and object storage is not an input.

Every table starts at 100 points and loses points for each problem the scan finds. The grade is the letter for the final score. The home chart counts tables per grade. It is not a size-weighted median. UI words map to letters: A Excellent, B Good, C Fair, D Poor, F Critical. There are two deduction sizes and no others: a warning costs 8 points and a critical finding costs 20. Two warnings and one critical is 100 − 8 − 8 − 20 = 64, grade C. The planner is engine-agnostic. Trino SQL and Spark SQL are rendered apart, so the same plan produces different SQL and never different intent.

Native Go compaction is a configured engine path and is not assumed to be on. The planner does not change shape for it. It receives the same plan as Trino and Spark, and runs the rewrite itself. Flink is not on this page. Cryo can emit a Flink maintenance config and does not submit the job.
